records.name: The Soapbox: Community Print Shop and Zine Library
records.summary: A print shop and zine library in West Philadelphia with public open hours on Wednesday evenings and Sunday afternoons. Members use the presses, and the studio teaches printmaking, bookmaking, and zine making.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member to use the presses after orientation and training, take a workshop, ask about a custom workshop or private lesson, or browse the free zine library.

schedule.text: Public open hours: Wednesdays 6 to 10 pm and Sundays 1 to 5 pm. Members have their own access times.

cost.text: Open Hours membership is $40 a month for working members or $50 a month for non-working members. Keyholder membership is $115 a month for working members or $135 a month for non-working members, with a three month minimum. A four visit punchcard is $75. Workshops charge their own fees.

access.notes: The site says the facilities are ADA accessible and the main entrance on Reinhard Street is accessible. It does not describe stairs, elevators or restrooms. For other accommodations, email studio@phillysoapbox.org.

first_step.how: Call the studio phone at (267) 630-1632 during Wednesday 6 to 10 pm or Sunday 1 to 5 pm open hours to ask about a visit, and apply for a membership if you want to use the equipment.
first_step.basis: Studio access takes a membership, a punchcard or a workshop, plus an application and an orientation before you use the presses. The open hours are posted, but the site does not say a visitor can walk in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Open hours run on Wednesday evenings and Sunday afternoons, with monitors who answer questions but do not teach. Entry takes a membership, a punchcard or a workshop, and you call the studio to be let in. Newer members must finish set training hours on each press or tool before they use it.
first_visit_tips: Call the studio phone during open hours to be let in: (267) 630-1632.
Masks are encouraged but optional in the studio, according to the site.
Use the main entrance on Reinhard Street, which the site describes as accessible.
Email studio@phillysoapbox.org before you come if you need an accommodation.

records.notes: Hours conflict: the homepage says keyholders have 24/7 studio access, while the membership page says 8 am to 10 pm seven days, so no keyholder hours are recorded. The workshops page says studio access needs a membership, a workshop or volunteering. Zine library visitor rules are not on the site. Soapbox Fellows volunteer five hours a week for six months in exchange for keyholder access, with applications reviewed in March and September. Riso Expo 2026 and Philly Zine Fest are named but undated. Named partners The Rotunda, Temple University and Philly Zine Fest were not added as leads: venue, university and festival, not community groups.

records.name: Soil Generation
records.summary: A collective of Black and Brown women and gender-expansive people who work on access to land, growing food, and healing, with campaigns on urban farming and climate justice.
records.what_you_do: Email to ask for an invitation to the listserv, follow the group on Instagram or Facebook for campaign news, or donate. The group is not recruiting volunteers right now and publishes no meetings or classes.

schedule.text: No meetings, classes or volunteer shifts are published. Campaigns and projects are announced on the website and social media.

cost.text: No membership fee is listed. Donations are optional, and the site's PayPal donate button says donations are tax-deductible.

first_step.how: Follow Soil Generation on Instagram, then email soilgen215@gmail.com to say who you are and what you are interested in, and ask for an invitation to the listserv.
first_step.basis: The group is not recruiting volunteers now, and its listserv is by invitation on request, aimed at Black and Brown community members. The way in is unclear, so a first timer has to ask first.
first_step.what_to_expect: There are no set meetings, classes or shifts to attend. The collective shares its campaigns, such as the urban agriculture plan and the threatened gardens campaign, plus cultural projects like a manual and a short film, through its website and social media. Garden visits are not offered right now because the group has no growing space open to visitors.
first_visit_tips: Say who you are and what you are interested in when you write, since the group asks for this.
Follow Instagram or Facebook for campaign news, because the newsletter sign-up page shows a note that its storage is not set up yet.
Do not plan a garden visit; the group has no growing space open to visitors right now.

records.notes: Tier 1 had kind nonprofit. The contact page calls the group a relationship-based collective, not a formal organization, so kind is network. Speaking requests are reviewed case by case, with priority to existing relationships and to people of color. The site says Black and Brown women and gender-expansive people; no community tag exists for Brown or gender-expansive, so the record uses women and black. The site has no dated news. The resource guide article on the homepage is undated. The garden groups it suggests for volunteering are in leads_only.

records.name: Sons of Ben
records.notes: Set to out_of_area for owner decision. Matches are at Subaru Park in Chester, PA, outside Philadelphia, and the group's charity support names the Chester area. Nothing read shows it meets in or serves Philadelphia. If the owner wants Philadelphia Union supporter groups listed, this can change to publish with a non-city location. Membership is $35 for new members and $30 for returning members, annual dues paid through the club's BigCartel storefront per the FAQ. The home page JOIN button goes to a 2026 givebutter page, so check which one before paying. Directions name the SEPTA Wilmington/Newark Regional Rail to Chester Transportation Center, plus a free shuttle on match days.

records.name: South Philadelphia Community Fridge
records.summary: Volunteers who keep community fridges stocked with donated food at several sites across South Philadelphia. The fridges are open around the clock for anyone who needs food.
records.what_you_do: Stock the fridges with donated food, help collect food from grocers and restaurants, or drive large donations to fridges and pantries. You can also host a food drive.

schedule.text: Fridges are open around the clock. The site lists no set volunteer shifts; volunteers help when they are free.

cost.text: Taking food is free. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Fill in the Volunteer With Us form linked from the Take Action page to join a stocking or collection shift, or email southphlcommunityfridge@gmail.com with questions first.
first_step.basis: The Take Action page says anyone can volunteer and gives an open sign-up form. It describes no training and no set shifts, and it does not single out newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers stock and clean the fridges, meet food drivers who bring donations, and drive large donations to other fridges and pantries. There are no set shifts or training described, so you pick the time that works for you. The site says anyone can volunteer.
first_visit_tips: Email southphlcommunityfridge@gmail.com with questions about volunteering, locations or partnerships, as the About page suggests.
Use the address list on the website to find the fridge nearest you.
The site lists no shift times, so ask the group when the next stocking shift is planned.

records.notes: Eight fridge addresses come from the home page. The Take Action page says the fridges are open 24/7. The group file says nonprofit, but the group is a volunteer network fiscally sponsored by The Hack Foundation, so kind is network, as in the batch file. An eighth fridge at Universal Audenried High School has no address on the site and is not listed. The news page lists media coverage back to 2020; the newest item is dated February 18, 2026. Donations go through a Target gift registry link and a donation page at hcb.hackclub.com. The Host a Food Drive page gives food drive guidance separately. The footer year 2025 is not used as evidence.

records.name: South Philly Striders Running Club
records.summary: A free running club for South Philadelphia and nearby neighborhoods such as Queen Village, Old City and Society Hill. Runners of all abilities meet for weekday morning and Saturday runs, and each December the club joins a holiday lights run that ends at a brewery.
records.what_you_do: Show up at a scheduled run, such as the Tuesday or Thursday 6:15 am or Saturday 8 am runs from Front and South Streets, or join the December holiday lights run and the gathering at its finish.

schedule.text: Regular runs: Tuesday and Thursday at 6:15 am and Saturday at 8 am, all leaving Front and South Streets. Wednesday at 6:30 pm from 6th and Race Streets. The December holiday lights run starts at 7 pm from Marconi Plaza each year.

locations.label: Front and South Streets (Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday runs)
Marconi Plaza, Broad Street and Oregon Avenue (holiday lights run start)

cost.text: There is no membership fee or dues. The site lists no cost for the regular runs.

first_step.how: Show up at a Tuesday or Thursday 6:15 am, Wednesday 6:30 pm, or Saturday 8 am run, or email the club or message its Facebook group with questions first.
first_step.basis: The about page says newcomers are always welcome, there are no fees, and you can show up at a scheduled run. The holiday run page says all paces are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Typical weekday morning runs cover 2 to 7 miles, and Saturday runs range from 3 to 10 or more miles, according to the about page. Runners of all abilities are welcome, and there is no fee to join. The site names no pace groups or leaders, so ask in the Facebook group which run suits your pace before you come.
first_visit_tips: Meet at Front and South Streets for the morning runs, which the club lists as the start point.
Check the club's Facebook group for news on runs, since the site says other runs are posted there and on Instagram.
For the December holiday run, bring your ID and cross streets only on green lights, as the club asks.

records.notes: Tier 1 did not list the regular runs. The runs page lists Tuesday and Thursday at 6:15 am and Saturday at 8 am from Front and South Streets, plus a Wednesday 6:30 pm run from 6th and Race Streets that crosses the Ben Franklin Bridge (the page calls it the Travis Bridge Club run). The 2025 holiday lights run was Thursday, December 11, 2025, at 7 pm, finishing at Dock Street Brewery South; no 2026 post exists yet. Pace groups are not listed. Fishtown Beer Runners co-hosts the holiday run and is in leads_only.

records.name: Spells Writing Lab, Inc.
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps school-age children build creative and expository writing skills through free writing programs, classroom visits, and workshops for teachers.
records.what_you_do: Apply online to volunteer as a classroom writing mentor, a Write Club tutor (no teaching experience needed), or a workshop helper, then attend an orientation. You can also register for a workshop or ask for a classroom visit.

schedule.text: Write Club workshops run live online on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 11 am during the school year. Free workshops run on many weekend afternoons during the school year at the lab and at pop-up sites. Classroom mentors work in schools during the day, and volunteer orientations are usually on weeknights in Center City.

cost.text: The Write Club and the workshops are free for students. The site lists no cost to volunteers.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: the Market-Frankford Line to Girard station, about 3.5 blocks away, and the Route 15 trolley to Girard Avenue and 2nd Street, about 2.5 blocks away. Buses 57 and 5 also serve the area. The office is on the second floor, and visitors use a callbox to be buzzed up. The site does not mention an elevator or a step-free entrance.

first_step.how: Submit the online volunteer application on phillyspells.org, linked as Volunteer Now, then attend the next orientation once a date is posted.
first_step.basis: The Write Club tutor page says no teaching experience is required, offers tutor training, and pairs newcomers with experienced tutors. Orientation dates are not posted yet, so the next step has no date.
first_step.what_to_expect: Tutors guide young writers through creative and expository forms, with training first and a buddy system for newcomers. The Write Club runs live online on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 11 am and is free for students, while classroom mentors travel to schools to lead workshops in person. The site sets no minimum time commitment for tutors, but orientation comes first.
first_visit_tips: Watch the site's news and events pages for the next orientation date, since none is posted now.
Expect an online application first, and the site does not say whether you need a background check.
Orientations are usually on weeknights in Center City, with one planned on Drexel University's campus.
Classroom mentors work in schools during the day, and the site says daytime availability is wanted.

records.notes: The office is at 1417 N 2nd Street, Suite 22B, per the directions page, which replaces the tier 1 Center City location; orientations are usually in Center City. Orientation dates were not posted when checked. The Write Club is free and online for ages 7 to 12; the page does not say whether tutors attend each live session. Workshops are free, but no current workshop names or dates are listed. Email write@phillyspells.org is the address for workshop proposals. Classroom mentor clearances, background checks and minimum age are not on the pages read. The newest dated item is a 2025 Classroom Workshop flyer with no month, so no last_sign_of_life is recorded.

records.name: Spiral Q
records.summary: A Philadelphia arts group that uses public art and community projects to bring people, neighborhoods and causes together. It works through the year with students, neighbors and activists.
records.what_you_do: Take part in Peoplehood, the yearly community parade and pageant, through art builds, community sessions and rehearsals. You can also ask about volunteering, fill in an interest form to join the board or advisory council, or donate money or supplies.

schedule.text: Peoplehood is an annual parade and pageant, built over about six weeks of community sessions, art builds and rehearsals. The parade is held on a Saturday in the fall, with a rain date a week later.

locations.label: Spiral Q warehouse (art builds and community sessions)

cost.text: The site lists no cost to take part. Donations and supply gifts are welcome.

first_step.how: Fill in the Peoplehood participation list form on Spiral Q's site, or email community@spiralq.org or call 215-222-6979 to ask how to take part.
first_step.basis: Anyone can fill in the participation form, and the site invites neighbors, students and activists to take part. Open hours and regular events are not published, so timing depends on the project calendar.
first_step.what_to_expect: Peoplehood starts with community conversations and creative meetings, moves to art builds where people make puppets, banners and screen prints, and ends with a parade and a pageant in a park. The process runs about six weeks. The site lists no cost to take part and asks for donations and supplies.
first_visit_tips: Fill in the participation list form, since individuals join the list before they take part.
Read the Art Build info document linked on the Peoplehood page for space, accessibility and parking details.
The parade starts at The Paul Robeson House, 4951 Walnut Street, and the pageant takes place in Clark Park.

records.notes: The Peoplehood page gives the parade date as Saturday, November 7, 2025 (rain date November 14), while its title says 2026. The year is not moved; the status is active only because of that 2025 date, so check with the group. The homepage shows a Save the Date image for Peoplehood 2026. The Art Build info document covers space, accessibility and parking and was not read, so access is unknown. Staff and board are listed on the who we are page and are not copied here. Named partners Mural Arts, the School District of Philadelphia and Girard College are institutions and were not added as leads.

The page does not say how to sign up to volunteer; its linked volunteer opportunities page was not read. Named on Soil Generation's site.

leads_only.note: Named on Soil Generation's contact page as a garden to volunteer with, with no link given there. One search did not find a Philadelphia group of this name. Not checked further.
